messages:
maria.chen: Hi team — quick q on secrets onboarding. I got my Vault token but not sure how to request access to project-specific secrets (redis creds + stripe key) for my app. Who do I open a ticket with and is there a preferred service-account pattern?
ajay: @maria.chen welcome! File a secrets request via the onboarding form: https://redwood-internal/new-hire-secrets. That routes to eng-security + DevEx. Include project name, env (dev/stage/prod), resource list, and justification.
sam.x: Also call out the principal (user vs service account). For apps we prefer creating a <project>-app-<env>-sa and using Workload Identity / Kubernetes service accounts.
olivia: Heads-up: prod requests require owner + secops approvals and a rotation plan. Dev/stage can be faster with short-lived creds.
maria.chen: Thanks. Is there an automated TTL/rotation we should expect? Do we have lifecycle policies in Vault?
ajay: Yes — we push dynamic secrets where possible. DB creds are usually short-lived (default 1h) and auto-rotated. Static third-party API keys are stored with a documented rotation cadence — typically 90 days non-prod, 30 days prod, unless ownership dictates otherwise.
secops: @maria.chen for KMS/CMK requests: include whether you need envelope encryption or key-wrapping. CMKs are approved only for prod/regulatory workloads. Put the KMS ask in the same form and tag it "kms".
olivia: If this is for CI, list the pipeline service identity and minimal scopes. Avoid embedding user tokens in CI jobs — use Vault agent or short-lived creds.
maria.chen: Any example I can paste into the form?
sam.x: Use this template in the justification: "Service account: mktg-app-dev-sa; Secrets: redis-read, stripe-live; Access pattern: Vault Agent with AppRole; Rotation: redis dynamic creds (1h), stripe key rotated every 90d; Approvers: app-owner, secops." Keep it concise.
ajay: After submission, devex-bot will ack within ~30m and a secops reviewer should pick it up within 4-6 business hours for non-prod. Prod reviews may take 1-2 business days depending on approvers.
maria.chen: Great, submitting now — thanks!
devex-bot: Your secrets request #SR-2026-114 has been created and assigned to secops-team. Track: https://redwood-internal/requests/SR-2026-114 :white_check_mark:
secops: Also see the secrets runbook: https://intra.redwood/ops/secrets-runbook — includes emergency access procedure, manual rotation steps, and escalation contacts. Ping me if you need expedited review.
maria.chen: One last q — for local dev, should I store creds in my laptop keychain or use Vault agent?
olivia: Prefer the Vault dev agent or ephemeral creds with short TTLs. If you must persist something, use OS keychain (macOS/Windows credential manager) and never check secrets into git.
maria.chen: Awesome, that clears it up — really appreciate everyone helping :tada:
